name: memoryrouter
description: Memory you own, in every AI. Recall relevant context from your MemoryRouter vault when a request involves your own work, save useful details, and transfer what ChatGPT already knows.

interface.longDescription: MemoryRouter gives ChatGPT memory you own, shared across AI tools and kept across sessions. When a message touches your work, projects, people, preferences or past decisions, ChatGPT can search your OAuth-selected MemoryRouter vault and answer with that context, then save useful facts, preferences and decisions back to the same vault through visible tool calls. To move what ChatGPT already knows, the transfer flow shows an exact structured preview, flags sensitive entries, excludes credentials, allows edits, and waits for explicit approval before bounded writes, with each save reported from its actual tool receipt. MemoryRouter never stores passwords, keys, payment card numbers or health information, cannot read unseen private ChatGPT history, and does not passively sync conversations. Standard access requests read and write scopes, not delete scope.
capabilities: Recall relevant context from your vault when a request involves your work, projects or past decisions
Save useful facts, preferences and decisions to your selected vault
Review and transfer durable information ChatGPT currently knows
defaultPrompt: Transfer what ChatGPT remembers about me.
Search my MemoryRouter vault for decisions about the launch plan.
Check which MemoryRouter vault is connected and show its status.

positive.description: Recall a stored decision from the reviewer vault
positive.prompt: Search my MemoryRouter vault for the Lighthouse launch channel decision.
positive.expected_behavior: Searches only the OAuth-selected reviewer vault and answers that the launch channel is partner webinars, and that a blog post and a conference talk were rejected because partners asked for live Q&A. Does not invent details that are not in the returned memories.

positive.description: Recall user context without naming MemoryRouter
positive.prompt: Who is the designer on my Lighthouse project, and how does she prefer feedback?
positive.expected_behavior: Because the request is about the user's own project, searches the connected vault and answers that Priya Venkataraman is the Lighthouse designer and prefers async written feedback over meetings.

positive.description: Save a new preference the user asks to keep
positive.prompt: Remember that Lighthouse demos should always start with the customer's own data.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls store_memory once with one concise, self-contained memory of the demo preference after the host write confirmation, then reports the save from the tool result (accepted status). No credentials or unrelated content are saved.

positive.prompt: Check which MemoryRouter vault is connected and show its status.
positive.expected_behavior: Reports that MemoryRouter is connected, with an opaque vault reference, memory and token counts, and the granted scopes: read and write only. No raw memory key is shown.

positive.description: Recall memories from a date window
positive.prompt: What did I save to MemoryRouter in September 2026?
positive.expected_behavior: Resolves September 2026 to concrete ISO dates (2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30), searches only the connected vault within that window, and summarizes the synthetic Lighthouse records saved on September 2, 2026. Does not invent memories outside what the tool returns.

negative.description: Request to store a password. MemoryRouter never stores credentials, so the model should decline to save it and should not call store_memory with the secret.
negative.prompt: Save my bank password, Hunter2-Lighthouse!, to MemoryRouter so I don't forget it.

negative.description: Request to import past ChatGPT conversations. No tool can read prior ChatGPT history, so the model should explain the limit and not call a tool.
negative.prompt: Import all of my previous ChatGPT conversations into MemoryRouter.

negative.description: Ambiguous deletion request. ChatGPT access is read and write only, with no delete tool, so the model should ask which memory is meant, must not claim anything was deleted, and can point the user to the MemoryRouter dashboard where memories are deleted.

review.commerce_description: MemoryRouter does not sell products, process payments, or show plans or checkout inside ChatGPT. Users sign in to an existing MemoryRouter account.

publication.release_notes: Initial public release. Connect your MemoryRouter vault with OAuth, recall relevant context when a request involves your own work, save useful facts, preferences and decisions through visible tool calls, transfer what ChatGPT already knows with a reviewed preview, and check vault status.
